McLaren: McLaren’s latest tweak is a small wing‑let added to the front brake duct. It smooths the air around the brakes, keeping them cooler and giving the front end a bit more downforce, which translates to better corner‑entry grip. In practice, that should help the team extract a few extra tenths around the twisty sections of this weekend’s circuit.
Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari’s engineers have re‑shaped the car’s under‑floor – adjusting the fences, front floor edge and tunnel – to smooth the airflow and squeeze out a little extra grip, especially in the corners. They’ve also opened up the diffuser at the rear and added a fresh winglet on the rear wing to make the car more stable under braking and through high‑speed turns. Together, these tweaks should give the team a nicer balance and a bit more down‑force for the challenges of this weekend’s circuit.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull’s new front‑wing now carries a longer‑chord flap, which gives the car extra bite up front and lets the drivers push harder through the high‑speed corners at this weekend’s circuit. At the same time, the team has widened the cooling louvers, improving airflow to keep the power unit and brakes in their sweet spot for longer. Together, the changes should translate into more grip on lap‑up and a more stable temperature window, helping the team stay competitive and avoid any overheating‑related hiccups during the race.
